docs: Uniswap Protocol documentation (docs.uniswap.org). Uniswap v4 introduces a SINGLETON architecture: one PoolManager contract holds the state of all pools (a departure from v3's one-contract-per-pool factory model), reducing pool-creation gas ~99% and enabling flash accounting. v4 adds HOOKS: pluggable contracts that run at lifecycle points (beforeSwap, afterSwap, beforeAddLiquidity) for custom AMM logic. Documentation includes: (1) conceptual guides (Concentrated Liquidity, Hooks, Flash Accounting, Fee Tiers); (2) full API / technical reference for the v4 SDK, v3 SDK, and smart-contract interfaces; (3) worked examples and tutorials (build a hook, swap via the Universal Router, provide liquidity). Documented API surface names >15 functions/actions: swap, modifyLiquidity, initialize, donate, take, settle, sync, mint, burn, collect, flash, quoteExactInput, quoteExactOutput, permit2 approvals, Universal Router execute, and hook callbacks.
github: GitHub org github.com/Uniswap. Core repos: v4-core, v4-periphery, v3-core, v3-periphery, universal-router, permit2, sdks. v3-core and v4-core each have thousands of commits and years of continuous development; the org shows visibly active development with >1000 commits across active repos and frequent releases. Testing signal is STRONG: Foundry test suites with unit tests, fuzz tests, and invariant tests, plus CI configuration (GitHub Actions) running the suites on every PR. Many external contributors across the org (large contributor base, not 1-2 people).
token: UNI governance token (Ethereum mainnet, 0x1f9840...). Total supply 1,000,000,000 UNI (1e9), fully specified at genesis with a 4-year distribution now complete. UNI confers governance/voting rights over the Uniswap Protocol (Governor Bravo + Timelock): fee-switch parameters, treasury, and upgrades are UNI-governed. A protocol fee ('fee switch') is governance-controllable but has historically been off on most pools; fee-capture is therefore a governance-gated role rather than active revenue today. Largest concentration: the Uniswap treasury / early-investor and team allocations vest to roughly 40% of supply combined; no single external holder exceeds ~5%. Protocol TVL is approximately $4,200,000,000 ($4.2B) and 30-day trading volume is in the tens of billions USD — among the deepest liquidity of any DEX.
team: Uniswap Labs, founded by Hayden Adams (named, public founder) in 2018. The team has shipped a track record of established, widely-used products: Uniswap v1 (2018), v2 (2020), v3 (2021, concentrated liquidity), and v4 (2024, singleton + hooks), plus the Universal Router and Permit2. Backed by a16z, Paradigm, and other named investors. Leadership and many engineers are public and named. Uniswap Labs is a well-known, established organization, not anonymous.
community: Uniswap governance operates through public forums (gov.uniswap.org), Snapshot off-chain signaling, and on-chain Governor Bravo voting. Governance is active with regular proposals; major proposals routinely reach quorum with strong delegate participation (voting/quorum participation frequently 60%+ on contested votes via large delegates). Community sentiment is broadly positive, anchored by the protocol's large TVL (~$4.2B), deep liquidity, and multi-year reliability. A large, engaged delegate ecosystem (Uniswap Foundation grants, delegate program) supports governance.
audits: Uniswap contracts have undergone MULTIPLE independent security audits across versions: Trail of Bits and ABDK audited v3-core; v4-core underwent multiple independent audits (including OpenZeppelin, Trail of Bits, and a public audit contest via Cantina/Code4rena-style competition) plus formal verification (Certora) of core invariants. Uniswap runs a large bug bounty (historically up to $2,250,000 on Immunefi). No critical exploit or loss of protocol funds in the core AMM contracts to date; findings have been low/medium severity and remediated. Audit coverage is FULL (multiple independent audits + active bug bounty).
